name: Manasseh
description: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: Joseph called the firstborn Manasseh, forgetting, for God had made him forget all his toil and all his father's house; and the second called he Ephraim, fruitful, for God had caused him to be fruitful in the land of his affliction.

Jacob set that in place. When Joseph saw his father lay his right hand upon Ephraim's head it displeased him, and he tried to move it to Manasseh's head; but Jacob refused and said, his younger brother shall be greater than he; and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

points: Word came to Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick, and he took with him his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim to visit Jacob; and Israel strengthened himself and sat upon the bed.

note.label: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel

points: Thy two sons Ephraim and Manasseh, as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine. Jacob took Joseph's sons as his own, so the blessings that came upon Jacob's sons came upon Ephraim and Manasseh also; they became children of Israel, partakers of the same promises as the rest of the sons of Jacob.

note.label: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel

points: Let my name be named on them: this is why Ephraim and Manasseh are counted in the twelve tribes even though they are Joseph's children.

note.label: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

points: Israel thought he would never see Joseph's face, and God showed him his seed also. Joseph set Ephraim toward Israel's left hand and Manasseh toward his right, so the firstborn would get the right hand blessing; and Israel crossed his hands wittingly, guiding them knowingly, laying his right hand on Ephraim the younger.

note.label: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

points: Joseph set Manasseh toward Israel's right hand and Ephraim toward his left, but Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it upon Ephraim the younger, guiding his hands wittingly, for Manasseh was the firstborn.

note.label: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel

points: Ephraim was set above Manasseh because Ephraim became the head of the Northern Kingdom of Israel.

note.label: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel

points: In thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh; and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.

note.label: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel

points: Joseph dwelt in Egypt and lived an hundred and ten years, and saw the children of Ephraim of the third generation; the children of Machir the son of Manasseh were brought up upon Joseph's knees.

note.label: Genesis 50: The Burial of Jacob and the Forgiveness of Joseph

points: Moses gave unto the children of Gad and of Reuben and unto half the tribe of Manasseh the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land with the cities thereof, and they built their cities and folds for sheep.

note.label: Numbers 32: The Inheritance of Reuben and Gad on This Side Jordan

points: The children of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead and took it, and dispossessed the Amorite which was in it: they took them out of the land.

note.label: Numbers 32: The Inheritance of Reuben and Gad on This Side Jordan

points: The chief fathers of the families of Gilead of the tribe of Manasseh bring an issue rising out of what was already ruled in Numbers 27: when Zelophehad died in the wilderness with no sons, the Lord ruled that his inheritance pass to his daughters.

note.label: Numbers 36: The Inheritance of the Daughters of Zelophehad

points: Jair the son of Manasseh took all the country of Argob and called it after his own name, Bashan-havoth-jair, unto this day.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: His horns are like the horns of unicorns: two horns, Ephraim and Manasseh. With them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: the Most High used Ephraim and Manasseh as the heads to push the ten tribes over to this side of the world, as the account of the tribes taking counsel to go forth into a further country shows.

And they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh: the blessing on Jacob's grandsons was to grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth. The Most High gets geographic with it: they went from the east to the west and multiplied in the midst of the hemisphere, in Central America.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

points: The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh passed over armed before the children of Israel, about forty thousand prepared for war, keeping the word they gave Moses: suited for battle with their brethren before returning to enjoy their own land on the other side.

note.label: Joshua 4: The Twelve Stone Memorial

points: Them did Moses the servant of the LORD and the children of Israel smite, and Moses gave their land for a possession unto the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh. Look up a map of the Jordan river and the twelve tribes and you will see the split of where Reuben, Gad, and half Manasseh dwelt, on the east side of Jordan.

note.label: Joshua 12: The Thirty and One Kings

points: The land is to be divided only unto the Israelites: unto the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh, for the other two and a half tribes had already received theirs. It had already been told that these lands must be divided among our people.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

points: Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh by their families: from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og, and all the towns of Jair, threescore cities, pertaining unto the children of Machir the son of Manasseh.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

points: The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, therefore no part was given unto the Levites in the land, save cities to dwell in with their suburbs for their cattle and for their substance.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

points: There were also separate cities for the children of Ephraim among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.

note.label: Joshua 16: The Lot of the Children of Joseph

points: A lot goes into an allotment, a portion; there was a portion for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph. Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh and the father of Gilead, was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.

The Bible maps that even the enemies of Israel put together according to the scriptures show this history: Manasseh held Bashan and a portion by Gilead on the other side of Jordan. The so-called Cubans come from this tribe; this is their history that their enemies do not want them to know.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: There was also a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families, Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph.
Remember that Manasseh was the son of Joseph; Joseph had two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: Ten portions fell to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan which were on the other side of Jordan. On the map the Jordan river flows down through the land, and across the river sat Gilead and Bashan, the lands Manasseh already held.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: The daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons, just as the Lord commanded for the daughters of Zelophehad, and the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: The coast of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethah; Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but Tappuah itself on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: The coast descended to the river Kanah: southward of the river the cities were Ephraim's, and northward it was Manasseh's, the sea was his border, and they met together in Asher on the north and in Issachar on the east.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: Manasseh also had within Issachar and Asher the cities of Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach, and Megiddo with their towns, even three countries.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: Even though Israel conquered the majority of the land of Canaan, there were still areas the Canaanites kept possession of; the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities, but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: Manasseh had issues driving the Canaanites out, but Ephraim did it. The difference between the two brothers goes back to Genesis 48, where Israel blessed Joseph's sons and crossed his hands, guiding them wittingly, meaning he knew exactly what he was doing.

Ephraim being greater goes into Ephraim becoming the head of the ten tribes, the head of the kingdom of Samaria; and it was Ephraim that led the charge, with the help of Issachar and Manasseh, that brought the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere. The unicorn there is not a fairy tale horse; the original etymology goes into the rhinoceros.

The Zondervan compact Bible dictionary, a tool to add to your arsenal, says Ephraim and Manasseh seem to have been bitter rivals, Manasseh being the larger group, but Ephraim asserting the more vigorous leadership, though they seem to have held their land in common for a time. Vigorous means very passionate, sometimes rough; that is the spirit the children of Ephraim have.

In Judges 7 Manasseh went to war with the three hundred men and destroyed the Midianites though they were lower in numbers, because Christ gave them the victory; then in Judges 8 Ephraim was upset that they were not called to help in that war. Ephraim always had that leadership attribute, that military spirit.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: Gad and Reuben and the half tribe of Manasseh had already received their inheritance beyond Jordan on the east, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave them.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

points: They appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah; and on the other side Jordan by Jericho they assigned Bezer out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

points: The children of Gershon had thirteen cities out of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, and the children of Merari had twelve cities out of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun; all given by lot as the Most High commanded by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

points: The children of Gershon received Golan in Bashan out of the other half tribe of Manasseh to be a city of refuge for the slayer, four cities out of Issachar, four out of Asher, and out of Naphtali three, including Kedesh in Galilee, a city of refuge: thirteen cities in all.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

points: The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go into the country of Gilead, the land of their possession according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

points: When Phinehas and the princes heard the words of the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, it pleased them. Phinehas said, This day we perceive that the LORD is among us, because ye have not committed this trespass against the Lord.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

points: Tribe after tribe repeats the same failure: neither did Manasseh, nor Ephraim, nor Zebulun, nor Asher, nor Naphtali drive out the inhabitants of their cities, and the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the mountain.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The Lord commissions him: go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites; have not I sent thee? Gideon answers with his pedigree: my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house. That is a defeated mentality, and we all have to overcome it, because every one of us was called for a reason, to put a brick in for the kingdom.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed over Gilead and Manasseh, and passed over unto the children of Ammon.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh had valiant men able to bear buckler and sword and skillful in war, four and forty thousand seven hundred and threescore that went to war.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

points: The half tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land from Bashan unto Baal-hermon and mount Hermon, and they increased.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

points: God stirred up Pul, or Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, to carry away Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh. The northern kingdom was taken in waves, not all at once.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Because of this the Most High stirred up the spirit of Pul, that is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, who carried Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity unto this day.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

points: The Levites had no land inheritance like the rest of the tribes, so these cities and their suburbs are where they dwelt, given out of Judah, Simeon, Benjamin, Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: The sons of Naphtali are named, and the sons of Manasseh through his concubine, down to the line of Gilead.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 7: The Warrior Tribes

points: Some of Manasseh fell to David; they had come with the Philistines against Saul but did not help them, for the Philistine lords sent them away, fearing he would return to Saul at the jeopardy of their heads.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

points: Among them were Judah, Simeon, Levi with Jehoiada leader of the Aaronites, Benjamin the kindred of Saul, Ephraim, and the half tribe of Manasseh, along with the tribes beyond Jordan.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

points: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon. Notice they're calling Ephraim and Manasseh strangers. So there was some that loved the Lord. That's good; very important on the street.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Asa gathers Judah, Benjamin, and the strangers out of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, who fell to him in abundance when they saw the Most High was with him. These strangers are Israelites whose hearts turned back.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 15: The Covenant to Seek the Most High

points: Hezekiah wrote to Ephraim and Manasseh, from Beersheba to Dan, to keep the Passover at Jerusalem. Many laughed the letters to scorn, but some of Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Now that the temple is cleansed and the priests sanctified, Hezekiah sends letters to all Israel and Judah, even to Ephraim and Manasseh, calling them to keep the Passover at Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 30: The Great Passover

points: The posts pass from city to city through Ephraim and Manasseh to Zebulun, but the people laugh them to scorn and mock them, the same mockery Israel meets today when the truth is preached.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 30: The Great Passover

points: Many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun had not cleansed themselves, yet they ate the Passover.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun eat the Passover otherwise than it was written, but Hezekiah prays that the good Lord pardon everyone who prepares his heart to seek God, and the Lord hearkens and heals the people. Grace and mercy are present here in the Old Testament.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 30: The Great Passover

points: When the feast is finished, all Israel present goes out to the cities and breaks the images, cuts down the groves, and throws down the high places and altars throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 31: The Tithe Restored

points: Gilead is His, Manasseh is His, Ephraim is the strength of His hand, and Judah is His lawgiver; Moab is His washpot, over Edom He casts out His shoe.

note.label: Psalm 60: Through God We Shall Do Valiantly

points: God has spoken in His holiness: Gilead is His, Manasseh is His, Ephraim is the strength of His head, and Judah is His lawgiver. Judah being the lawgiver is a prophecy of Christ, from whom the sceptre and rulership shall not depart.

note.label: Psalm 108: My Heart Is Fixed

points: Manasseh shall be against Ephraim, and Ephraim against Manasseh, and together they shall be against Judah; for all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

note.label: Isaiah 9: For Unto Us a Child Is Born
